record.title: Lower-bound conjecture for the optimal cleanup threshold
record.statement:
Let $m_\mathrm{opt}(n)$ be the value of $m$ minimizing the long-run average search-plus-cleanup cost, and let $\widetilde m_\mathrm{opt}(n)$ minimize the corresponding approximate cost $\widetilde F(m)$ in the complete-memory, numbered-shelves model $\mathcal M_4$.

**Approximate-threshold conjecture.** We have

$$
m_\mathrm{opt}(n)\geqslant \widetilde m_\mathrm{opt}(n).
$$

The approximate problem is analyzed explicitly, with $\widetilde m_\mathrm{opt}(n)$ lying near $3\log_2(n)$. The conjecture asserts that this computable approximate threshold is a lower bound for the true optimal threshold; the paper reports numerical support, but no proof is given.
record.source_name: Kimball Martin and Krishnan Shankar, “How often should you clean your room?”, arXiv:1305.1984 (2014).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: The proposed sharp threshold for rainbow connection number at least three
record.statement:
Let $r$ be a fixed integer with $r\geqslant 3$. For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{rc}(G)$ denote its rainbow connection number, and define

$$
\mathcal{R}_r=\\{G:\mathrm{rc}(G)\leqslant r\\}.
$$

Set

$$
C=\frac{r^{r-2}}{(r-2)!},\qquad p(n)=\frac{\left(C\log n\right)^{1/r}}{n^{1-1/r}}.
$$

**Proposed threshold conjecture.** The function $p(n)$ is a sharp threshold for the graph property $\mathcal{R}_r$.

This proposes that, for fixed $r\geqslant 3$, the threshold for rainbow connection number at most $r$ differs from the threshold for diameter at most $r$, unlike the known case $r=2$. The paper proves that this function is an upper bound for the threshold, while the asserted sharp-threshold statement is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The pseudo-threshold conjecture for homomorphisms to odd cycles
record.statement: Let $G_{n,\frac{c}{n}}$ be the random graph with edge probability $\frac{c}{n}$, let $C_{2\ell+1}$ be the cycle of length $2\ell+1$, and let odd-girth denote the length of the shortest odd cycle. **Pseudo-threshold conjecture.** For any $\ell$, there is a $c_\ell>1$ such that, with high probability, $G_{n,\frac{c}{n}}$ has no homomorphism to $C_{2\ell+1}$ for $c>c_\ell$, and has either odd-girth $<2\ell+1$ or a homomorphism to $C_{2\ell+1}$ for $c<c_\ell$. This conjecture proposes a sharp transition, subject to the obstruction caused by short odd cycles, for homomorphisms from sparse random graphs to a fixed odd cycle.

record.title: The common connectivity-threshold conjecture for directed and strict undirected nearest-neighbour graphs
record.statement: Let the directed model and the strict undirected model be the nearest-neighbour graph models considered in the paper, with $n$ points and parameter $k$. An isolated vertex is a vertex with no in-edges; more generally, a concentrated cluster has sub-logarithmic size. **Common connectivity-threshold conjecture.** The barrier for connectivity in both the directed model and the strict undirected model is an isolated vertex, or a concentrated cluster of sub-logarithmic size, with no in-edges, and the connectivity thresholds in the two models are the same, at a value somewhat greater than $0.7209\log n$. The proved lower bound for the connectivity threshold is essentially the threshold for having a point with no in-edges; the conjecture identifies this phenomenon as the actual obstruction to connectivity in both models.

record.title: Critical thresholds for critical-number-two binary matroids
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be the class of simple binary matroids of critical number $2$. For $\delta\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12\}$, let $\mathcal{N}_\delta$ be the three subclasses defined in the source according to the existence and properties of a $1$-codimensional independent subspace. **Critical-number-two threshold conjecture.** For each $\delta\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12\}$, every matroid in $\mathcal{N}_\delta$ has critical threshold $\delta$. This is the first case of the paper's proposed classification of critical thresholds; it is not resolved in the source.

record.title: Critical threshold formula for higher critical number
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a simple binary matroid of critical number $c\geq 2$. A $k$-codimensional subspace of $N$ is obtained by intersecting its ground set, in a projective-geometry representation, with a flat of rank $r(N)-k$. Let $\mathcal{N}_0$, $\mathcal{N}_{1/4}$, and $\mathcal{N}_{1/2}$ be the subclasses of critical-number-two simple binary matroids defined in the source. **Higher-critical-number threshold conjecture.** The critical threshold of $N$ is

$$
1-(1-\delta)2^{2-c},
$$

where $\delta\in\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12\}$ is minimal such that $N|S\in\mathcal{N}_\delta$ for some $(c-2)$-codimensional subspace $S$ of $N$. This conjecture is stated to imply the simplified threshold-values conjecture and remains open in the source.

record.title: Geelen and Nelson's critical threshold conjecture for matroids
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a matroid, let $\chi(N)$ denote its critical number, and let its critical threshold be the infimum of the density thresholds forcing bounded critical number. **Geelen and Nelson's conjecture.** If $\chi(N)\geq 2$, then the critical threshold of $N$ is

$$
1-i\cdot2^{-\chi(N)}
$$

for some $i\in\\{2,3,4\\}$. The lower bound is known, while the matching upper-threshold description remains open in general.

record.title: Alphabet-independence conjecture for the threshold avoiding powers and anti-powers
record.statement: Let $N_\alpha(k,k)$ denote the quantity defined in the paper as the relevant threshold for words over an alphabet of size $\alpha$, avoiding $k$-powers and $k$-anti-powers. **Alphabet-independence conjecture.** The quantity $N_\alpha(k,k)$ is independent of $\alpha$. The few known values suggest this possible structural property of the set of words avoiding $k$-powers and $k$-anti-powers that achieve the length $N_\alpha(k,k)$ for arbitrary alphabet sizes; the conjecture is presented as an open direction.

record.title: Empty-intersection conjecture for copies of complete graphs above the Turán threshold
record.statement:
Let $V_1,V_2,\ldots,V_{k-1}$ be the vertex classes of the balanced Turán graph $T_{k-1}(n)$, with sizes satisfying $\left\lceil\frac n2\right\rceil\geq |V_1|\geq\cdots\geq |V_{k-1}|\geq\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor$ and $\sum_i|V_i|=n$. Let $T_{k-1}^{\sqsubset}$ be obtained from $T_{k-1}(n)$ by adding an edge $\{x,y\}$ in $V_1$, adding an edge $\{u,v\}$ in $V_2$, and deleting the edge $\{u,x\}$. **Empty-intersection conjecture.** If a graph on $n$ vertices has $t_{k-1}(n)+1$ edges and the copies of $K_k$ have empty intersection, then the number of copies of $K_k$ is at least the number in $T_{k-1}^{\sqsubset}$, namely

$$
(|V_2|-1)|V_3|\cdot|V_4|\cdots|V_{k-1}|+(|V_1|-1)|V_3|\cdot|V_4|\cdots|V_{k-1}|=(|V_1|+|V_2|-2)|V_3|\cdot|V_4|\cdots|V_{k-1}|.
$$

This would generalize the paper's theorem for triangles, but the source gives no resolution and presents it as an open problem.

record.title: Conjecture that the two-uniform threshold equals $\log 2$
record.statement:
Let $\xi_m(2)$ denote the threshold parameter arising from the asymmetric choosability of complete bipartite graphs when $k_A=2$.

**Two-uniform threshold conjecture.**

$$
\xi_m(2)=\log 2.
$$

The source proves the bounds $\frac12\log 3\leq\xi_m(2)\leq\log 2$ and argues that equality at the lower bound is unlikely based on the equality structure in an auxiliary probabilistic estimate. The conjecture asserts that the upper bound is sharp.

record.title: The regularity-threshold conjecture for random Steiner complexes
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a random $k$-regular $d$-complex on $n$ vertices, and let $k(d)=4d^2+d+2$ denote the threshold appearing in Theorem 1. The theorem currently assumes $k>k(d)$.

**Regularity-threshold conjecture.** The condition on $k$ in Theorem 1 can be improved to

$$
k>d+1.
$$

The bound $k>d+1$ is suggested by the fact that for $k<d+1$, the upper Laplacian $\Delta_{d+1}^+(X)$ has a non-trivial zero eigenvalue and hence the simplicial matrix-tree theorem gives $\kappa_d(X)=0$. The conjecture asks whether the stronger regularity hypothesis arising from Garland's method can be reduced to this natural threshold.

record.title: The positive-density large-triangle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of positive upper density, and let $u,v,w\in\mathbb{R}^2$ be non-collinear points. A configuration congruent to a finite set means an image of that set under a Euclidean isometry. **Large-triangle conjecture.** There exists $l_0>0$ such that, for every $l\geq l_0$, the set $A$ contains a configuration congruent to

$$
\{lu,lv,lw\}.
$$

This is the simplest case of the paper's proposed extension of positive-density configuration results from non-degenerate configurations with at most $d$ points to configurations containing $d+1$ points. The source describes it as an obvious question left open by earlier results, and no resolution is supplied.

record.title: Growth constant at the logarithmic genus threshold
record.statement:
Let $g$ be a genus function and let $\mathcal A^g$ be one of the labelled graph classes considered in the paper. **Logarithmic-threshold growth-constant conjecture.** If $c>0$ is a constant and

$$
g(n)\sim \frac{cn}{\log n},
$$

then $\mathcal A^g$ has a growth constant $\gamma=\gamma(c)$. This concerns the boundary regime where the radius of convergence is positive, but the paper does not establish existence of a growth constant.
record.source_name: Colin McDiarmid and Sophia Saller, “Classes of graphs embeddable in order-dependent surfaces”, arXiv:2106.06775 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06775

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Conjecture on the perturbed threshold for the third power of a Hamilton cycle at density one quarter
record.statement:
For $chat{p}_{calpha}(n)$, the perturbed threshold for containment of the third power of a Hamilton cycle in the randomly perturbed graph model, the relevant density parameter is $calpha=1/4$.

**Threshold conjecture.** The perturbed threshold satisfies

$$
\hat{p}_{1/4}(n)=n^{-1/2}.
$$

The preceding discussion establishes the lower bound $chat{p}_{1/4}(n)\ge n^{-1/2}$ by reducing containment to finding the square of a Hamilton cycle on $3n/4$ vertices, and conjectures that this lower bound is tight. The source does not provide a proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Julia Böttcher, Olaf Parczyk, Amedeo Sgueglia and Jozef Skokan, “The square of a Hamilton cycle in randomly perturbed graphs”, arXiv:2202.05215 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05215

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: The degree-three threshold conjecture for leaf joined trees
record.statement:
Let $\Delta_0$ be the threshold parameter in Theorem~, concerning the accumulation of chromatic zeros of leaf joined trees relative to the degree bound $\Delta$. **The degree-three threshold conjecture.** Theorem~ remains true when

$$
\Delta_0=3.
$$

The conjecture is supported by numerical data for leaf joined trees and is related to questions on zeros of independence polynomials of bounded-degree graphs. The source provides no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Ferenc Bencs, Jeroen Huijben and Guus Regts, “On the location of chromatic zeros of series-parallel graphs”, arXiv:2204.10038 (2023).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

record.title: Threshold conjecture for third-order Turán inequalities and invariant positivity
record.statement:
Let $p(n)$ and $\bar{p}(n)$ denote the partition functions considered in the paper, let $\Delta^k$ denote the $k$-th finite-difference operator, and let $I$ denote the invariant used in the paper. For $1\leq k\leq 5$, write $T_p(k)$, $T_{\bar{p}}(k)$, $I_p(k)$, and $I_{\bar{p}}(k)$ for the proposed thresholds.

**Threshold conjecture.** For $1\leq k\leq 5$, $\Delta^k p(n)$, respectively $\Delta^k\bar{p}(n)$, satisfies the third-order Turán inequality whenever $n\geq T_p(k)$, respectively $n\geq T_{\bar{p}}(k)$. Moreover, $\Delta^k p(n)$, respectively $\Delta^k\bar{p}(n)$, satisfies $I>0$ whenever $n\geq I_p(k)$, respectively $n\geq I_{\bar{p}}(k)$.

These conjectures give explicit threshold ranges for two further positivity properties of finite differences of the partition functions. The source specifies the proposed thresholds in tables, while the validity of the assertions remains open.
record.source_name: Eve Y. Y. Yang, “Laguerre inequalities and determinantal inequalities for the finite difference of the partition functions”, arXiv:2312.10909 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.10909

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Conjecture on the critical intensity thresholds in the soft Boolean model
record.statement:
Let $\beta_c(\gamma,0,\delta)$ be the critical intensity and let $\widetilde{\beta}_c$ be the critical intensity of Theorem~. **Critical-intensity equality conjecture.**

$$
\widetilde{\beta}_c=\beta_c(\gamma,0,\delta)=\beta_1(\gamma,0,\delta).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the threshold controlling the proof coincides with the actual subcritical critical intensity, so the tail behaviour should remain unchanged throughout the subcritical regime. It strengthens the preceding conjecture that $\widetilde{\beta}_c\geq\beta_1(\gamma,0,\delta)$; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Benedikt Jahnel, Lukas Lüchtrath and Marcel Ortgiese, “Cluster sizes in subcritical soft Boolean models”, arXiv:2404.13730 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13730

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Narayanan–Schacht conjecture on the threshold for non-linear Hamilton cycles
record.statement:
Let $G_r(n,p)$ be the random $r$-uniform hypergraph, and let $C^{(r)}_{n,\ell}$ be the $r$-uniform $\ell$-cycle on $n$ vertices. Write $Z(C^{(r)}_{n,\ell})$ for the number of copies of $C^{(r)}_{n,\ell}$ in $G_r(n,p)$. For integers $r>\ell>1$, assume $(r-\ell)\mid n$. **Narayanan–Schacht conjecture.** If $p=p(n)$ satisfies

$$
\mathbb{E}[Z(C^{(r)}_{n,\ell})]\longrightarrow\infty,
$$

then

$$
\Pr\bigl[C^{(r)}_{n,\ell}\subset G_r(n,p)\bigr]\longrightarrow 1.
$$

Narayanan and Schacht proved that the first-moment threshold is sharp, but above that threshold the expected number of cycles can already be exponentially large. The conjecture asks whether divergence of the expectation alone suffices for the appearance of a non-linear Hamilton cycle with high probability.
record.source_name: Byron Chin, “Exact threshold and limiting distribution for non-linear Hamilton cycles”, arXiv:2411.13452 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: Hutchcroft's weighted-amenability threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Gamma$ be a closed subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ acting transitively on $G$, and let $\mathbf{w}$ be the induced relative weight function. Let $p_h(G,\Gamma)$ be the heavy-cluster threshold and let $p_u(G)$ be the uniqueness threshold. **Hutchcroft's conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $\mathbf{w}$-amenable if and only if

$$
p_h(G,\Gamma)=p_u(G).
$$

This is presented as a generalization of the Benjamini–Schramm conjecture relating amenability to equality of percolation thresholds. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Grigory Terlov and Ádám Timár, “Weighted-amenability and percolation”, arXiv:2502.02560 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02560

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2025). “Finally, this conjecture was resolved for graphs whose automorphism group contains a nonunimodular subgroup acting quasi-transitively .”

record.title: The truncate-and-relax algorithm's threshold conjecture for hypergraph community recovery
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be the hypergraph stochastic block model with community assignment $\sigma$, let $\widehat{\Sigma}(\mathcal{H})$ denote the semidefinite-programming estimator, and let $I_2(\alpha,\beta)$ be the threshold function defined by

$$
I_2(\alpha,\beta) = \max_{t\geq 0} 
\frac{1}{2^{k-1}}\left[ \alpha (1-e^{-(k-1)t}) + \sum_{a=1}^{k-1} \beta \binom{k-1}{a} \left(1-e^{-(k-1-2a)t}\right)\right].
$$

**The truncate-and-relax threshold conjecture.** If $I_2(\alpha,\beta) > 1$, then

$$
\widehat{\Sigma}(\mathcal{H}) = \sigma\sigma^T
$$

with probability $1-o_n(1)$. The conjecture proposes that $I_2(\alpha,\beta)=1$ is the correct performance threshold for the truncate-and-relax algorithm; the cited theorem establishes failure below the threshold and success of the truncated estimator above it, but does not establish success of the full semidefinite-programming estimator.
record.source_name: Chiheon Kim, Afonso S. Bandeira and Michel X. Goemans, “Stochastic Block Model for Hypergraphs: Statistical limits and a semidefinite programming approach”, arXiv:1807.02884 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.02884

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).
